captured_state.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
captured_state.sso_connector_setup_note: SSO connectors (OIDC and SAML) are pre-configured pointing to a mock IdP. The mock IdP is controllable: POST /admin/set-claims to change identity attributes (sub, email, name, groups, email_verified).

finding.sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge: local password user then SAML SSO login with same email but different upstream principal (NameID/sub). Verify they do NOT collapse into one identity when email is verified (tests over-aggressive email-based linking).
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-protocol account linking occurred: SAML SSO login (different upstream principal) was merged into the existing local password user solely based on the same verified email, enabling potential account takeover if an attacker controls an IdP asserting that email.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cross-protocol account linking occurred: SAML SSO login (different upstream principal) was merged into the existing local password user solely based on the same verified email, enabling potential account takeover if an attacker controls an IdP asserting that email.

sequence.description: Cross-protocol identity merge: local password user then SAML SSO login with same email but different upstream principal (NameID/sub). Verify they do NOT collapse into one identity when email is verified (tests over-aggressive email-based linking).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I4: A password principal and an enterprise SSO principal with the same email but different upstream subject must not collapse into the same downstream subject unless explicitly intended and safely bound; over-aggressive linking can cause identity boundary loss.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
